negative_reviews.author: M. the customer
negative_reviews.text: I would no recommend the ramen. Takoyaki and chicken teriyaki were good!

negative_reviews.author: Zhi Chang
negative_reviews.text: Great atmosphere and good selection of food! Navin was our server and our experience was great.

negative_reviews.author: Shams Al-Fekaiki
negative_reviews.text:
honestly the worst meal I’ve had in a long time, I ordered the chicken Yaki Soba and it was so horrible and almost inedible, I even think a supermarket microwave meal would have tasted better. I ate some of it because I was very but I’m not sure how they could have messed up noodles…

The other meals on the tables across from mine looked nice so maybe I just ordered the wrong thing.

The service was really inattentive, forgetting things when asked. Noticed there was over 12 full tables and only 2 waiters. The intense fluorescent pink light is really off putting when you’re eating. I wouldn’t recommend

deliveroo.source: sales + orders: Deliveroo Tax Invoice PDF (Total Order Value), issued 19/10/2026 + ops from Weekly Summary sheet

issues: Covers rose by 193 (16.25%) week on week and spend per head fell by £0.97, which the site put down to the SLL 50% discount and £5 ramen promotions, with guests ordering cheap ramen and fewer drinks.

Sales rose by £2,624.69 (10.05%) week on week and were £5,201.21 (22.22%) above target, with Thursday to Saturday getting busy; Ziang Lin called it a record week of £28,000 (up 22%) despite heavy discounting alongside SLL.
It was unclear whether the SLL promotion ended last week; Ziang Lin will check with Matt and said the discount will be reinstated if sales drop further.
Food and drinks variance was 7.3% (food 8.9%, wet minus 3.8%), an unexpected food variance jump from 3.5% to 8.9%.
Labour was 24.18%.
Google rating for the week was 5.00.

Deliveroo late prepared orders rose while prep times fell, and the Deliveroo rating dipped to 4.4 after 1 star reviews about too little katsu curry sauce, an added egg mistake, cutlery and curry portions; a yakisoba issue was also reviewed.
Chicken katsu curry was out of stock and due back on 21/10.
To lift the Deliveroo rating back to 4.5, Ziang Lin suggested adding a free Japanese lemonade or aloe vera bottle with a thank you sticker to Deliveroo orders.

A customer complained about being questioned over a request to remove the service charge for religious reasons; Ziang Lin called and apologised and emailed an offer of free food, and any returning customer presenting that email must be treated with the utmost respect and given a full meal on the house.
A dripping draft beer pipe is causing a strange smell at the bar, so the bar needs a deep clean this week and the leak source must be found.
Shoreditch sold 168 edamame portions in a week, more than all other South England sites combined.

Staffing: Dipen has joined as part time sushi; staff are moving down from Edinburgh, including Louisa and possibly another system manager or full time FOH; new sushi chef training hours for shadowing and learning the menu are paid at £13.50 per hour.
Ziang Lin asked for the rota to be released by Wednesday instead of Friday.

Areas for improvement: take payment first for takeaway orders and have a card machine at the main door; upsell edamame, draft beer rounds and chicken karaage; pour hot water at the table; and cross train sushi chefs on the bar and greeting customers during quiet sushi times.
Upcoming: every weekend is a Town Hall event.
The site is working on payroll.
Ziang Lin and Kaitlin Docherty plan to swap sites at the end of the month, with Ziang Lin working in Soho three days a week and Kaitlin Docherty covering Shoreditch and Southampton.

Region: the team aligned on implementing and keeping the dry ice presentation standard for volcano rolls and sashimi across sites: dry ice is poured at the table in a circular shape for volcano rolls, and sashimi is served on crushed ice in a red vegan ramen bowl with bamboo leaves and daikon to reduce dry ice waste.
Saturday sales have grown from about £1,000 to £2,000 to about £4,000 to £5,000 (AM Updates 21/10).
Food cost was 28.10% despite a missing sous vide chicken delivery, which Jerry and Remy need to address, and spend per head was £20 (AM Updates 21/10).

The 1 star yakisoba review came from a busy £5,500 net Thursday when the chef batch cooked tickets, causing 20 to 30 minute delays and poor quality, and bland chicken ramen caused high customer wastage (AM Updates 21/10).
Teddy Lee praised the use of excess drinks dry ice for sushi presentation as resourceful chef initiative (AM Updates 21/10).
Region: Michael made rider wait time the priority delivery metric this week, followed by ratings; sites need a 4.7 Deliveroo rating to compete and open times above 99.5% (AM Updates 21/10).
Region: GMs and head chefs must run a daily morning brief for FOH and BOH using the app's daily tab to review sales, delivery ratings and setups (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: failed delivery orders come from items marked out of stock on Kobas but not on Deliverect, so managers must update both, snooze unavailable extras by PLU and check Deliverect failed order statuses daily (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: stock edit permissions will be suspended for one week to see true variances, after wastage and comps were used to bring variances under 5% and distort Kobas ordering baselines (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: from next week automated Gemini meeting recordings and dashboard sign offs replace manual meeting notes and KPI sheets, with tasks synced to Asana and the legacy spreadsheets kept as a backup for now (AM Updates 21/10).
Region: third party discounted bookings are no longer allowed on Saturdays and are capped at a share of capacity on other days (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: Hungry Panda still has untranslated menu text, wrong integrations and overridden PLUs; Sophie is to fix the setup, and Michael suggested turning it off if it hurts Deliveroo and Slerp without enough revenue (AM Updates 21/10).
